why: By shortening C4/C6 and swapping/removing examples, the prompt became more permissive about chopping off very short continuations and placing cuts adjacent to heads: that produced small gains for tiny pieces (≤3 tokens) but caused more harmful splits in the ≤5 bin where essential complements or verb–argument material were severed (e.g. turning 'that an immediate diagnosis cannot be made' into a fragment 'cannot be made').
lesson: When shortening guidance, preserve explicit prohibitions and clear examples that prevent cutting essential complements or splitting dependency heads, so brevity doesn't trade away constraints that protect short but necessary continuations.
